name: Raven
fun_fact: Koryak storytellers call him Kutkinnaku, Big Raven, and treat his greed and cunning as part of the making of the world.

name: Bear
role: Sacred ancestor and honoured guest of the bear ceremony
fun_fact: In Khanty and Mansi ceremony he is addressed as a guest and asked to forgive the hunters, not treated as mere game.

name: Shaman
role: Ritual specialist who travels between worlds
fun_fact: The drum is often called a mount or boat, because the shaman is said to ride it into other worlds.

name: Spirit Master
role: Master spirit who owns a place, a species or a herd
fun_fact: Hunters speak of master spirits as owners or wardens of animals, and they negotiate with them rather than command them.

name: Reindeer
role: Companion and kin of the herding family
fun_fact: Reindeer are the only deer domesticated in the Arctic, and herders follow their migrations rather than penning them.

name: Hunter
role: Human who negotiates with the taiga and its animals
fun_fact: In many Siberian tales the hunter survives by patience and respect for the animal, not by strength alone.

name: Sun
role: Luminous being of the upper world
fun_fact: Sakha communities greet the sun at Yhyakh, the summer solstice festival, with kumys and circular dances.

name: Moon
role: Luminous being of the night sky
fun_fact: Some Buryat and Sakha tellings explain the moon's weaker light as the result of a wound or a punishment.

name: Ice Giant
role: Personification of cold who carries winter with him
fun_fact: In the tales his body may become a ridge, a frozen lake or a river valley, explaining the shape of the land.

name: Fire Keeper
role: Guardian of the hearth and its flame
fun_fact: The hearth fire is often treated as a living presence, fed before meals and consulted in small household rites.
